title: Facebook: The Inside Story
author: Steven Levy
note: Selected: technology writer Luke Dormehl includes it among the best technology books of 2020; Brad Stone's endorsement is publisher-reproduced. Goodreads 4.06/3,028 supports broad positive reader reception. Historical explanation of a technology company, not marketing instruction or partisan mobilization. Access to leadership is an evidence advantage and a possible source of bias; critical reader reports are retained rather than equating access with neutrality. No serious veto established. Global influence prevents the American-focus deduction; media distribution and platform power warrant T12=-10. This describes the company through 2019, not its current state.
notes: Extensive interviews support organizational history; leadership access can distort attribution of responsibility.
Connects product design, growth incentives, acquisitions, privacy and institutional responses.
Shows how growth targets and concentrated control shape decisions and neglected risks.
Explains organizational incentives more fully than the technical architecture.
D=7.5, moderate confidence from professional reviews and varied reader reports. Acquisitions and privacy decisions add different cases; lengthy founder narrative has lower yield. No full-text audit.
Historical decisions remain useful, though the platform and regulation continue to change.
Strong technology-organization fit with substantial media and political material.
Experienced technology reporter with broad access and favorable industry reception.
Readable and coherent company history despite its length.
Clear prose; interpretation is less certain than the documented events.
